_meta.note: context_dependent entries use default_if_uncertain until intent-aware logic (Phase 2) is added

PERSONAL_IDENTITY.reasoning: Rarely needed verbatim for the AI to complete a task

CONTACT_INFO.reasoning: Contact details rarely affect response quality

GOVERNMENT_ID.reasoning: No legitimate AI task requires the raw ID number itself

FINANCIAL_INFO.reasoning: Structured, sometimes needed in obfuscated form for validation-type tasks

AUTHENTICATION.reasoning: Never has a legitimate reason to reach a third-party AI

EMPLOYEE_DATA.reasoning: Sensitive HR context, sometimes needed (e.g. drafting a review) - encryption keeps it reversible

CUSTOMER_DATA.reasoning: Often needed in context (e.g. support-ticket drafting) but must stay reversible and controlled

HEALTH_DATA.reasoning: Diagnosis/medication info is very often the actual substance of the AI request

LEGAL_DATA.reasoning: Legal analysis tasks usually require the actual clause/document content

SOURCE_CODE.reasoning: Code structure/logic is usually the point of the request; embedded secrets are blocked separately by AUTHENTICATION/DATABASE_INFO/CLOUD_CREDENTIALS categories before this rule applies

DATABASE_INFO.reasoning: Connection strings/env files nearly always embed credentials

INFRASTRUCTURE.reasoning: Reveals attack surface / internal topology if leaked

BUSINESS_STRATEGY.reasoning: Competitively sensitive, but sometimes AI needs the content to help draft/refine

FINANCIAL_REPORT.reasoning: Needed for financial-analysis tasks, but must never leave the org unprotected

INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY.reasoning: Sometimes genuinely needed for AI assistance, but the highest-value org data - must be tightly protected and short-TTL

COMPANY_CONFIDENTIAL.reasoning: Broad catch-all; sensitivity varies heavily by actual content, not just the label

CLOUD_CREDENTIALS.reasoning: Direct infrastructure compromise risk if leaked

CRYPTO_KEYS.reasoning: Same as cloud credentials - irreversible compromise risk

AI_LLM_SPECIFIC.reasoning: A company's own system prompts / fine-tuning data are proprietary IP, but often exactly what the user is asking about

PUBLIC_INFORMATION.reasoning: Already public - no protection needed, would only degrade response quality
